source.title: Some of my favorite open problems

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit ball in R^3, let λ_1=π^2 be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -Δ on Ω, and consider smooth solutions u:Ω→R of -Δu=u^5+λu in Ω with u=0 on ∂Ω. For parameters 0<λ≤λ_1/4, does this boundary-value problem admit a nontrivial solution u not identically equal to 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1.1 (Implicit in [30]). Assume that (1.2) 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4. Does there exist a solution u ≢ 0 of (1.1)?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R^2 and, for ε>0, consider the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet problem -Δu=(1/ε^2)u(1-|u|^2) in Ω with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω. Let U_ε(x)=(x/|x|)f_ε(|x|) denote the radial solution obtained from the unique ODE solution f_ε with f_ε(0)=0 and f_ε(1)=1. Is U_ε the only solution of this boundary-value problem?

evidence.quote: We will denote by Uε(x) the solution of (2.1) given by (2.2)–(2.3), and we call it the radially symmetric (or just the radial) solution of (2.1). A long-standing open problem is whether Uε(x) is also the unique solution of (2.1). Open Problem 2.1 ... Is the radial solution Uε the only solution of (2.1)?

accepted.question_text: For the same Ginzburg–Landau problem on the unit disc Ω⊂R^2 with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω, let E_ε(u)=(1/2)∫_Ω|∇u|^2 + (1/(4ε^2))∫_Ω(|u|^2-1)^2 and let U_ε be the radial solution. Is U_ε a global minimizer of E_ε on H^1_g(Ω;R^2) for every ε>0?
accepted.context_brief: Variational minimality of GL radial solution

evidence.quote: The intermediate range ε0 ≤ ε < 1/√λ1 is totally open. An easier question still unresolved is the following. Open Problem 2.2. Is Uε a minimizer of Eε on H1_g(Ω;R2) for any ε > 0?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R^2, fix p>2, and consider the p-Ginzburg–Landau energy E_{ε,p}(u)=(1/p)∫_Ω|∇u|^p + (1/(4ε^2))∫_Ω(|u|^2-1)^2 on W^{1,p}_g(Ω;R^2) with boundary data g(x)=x on ∂Ω. If u_ε is any minimizer or any critical point of E_{ε,p}, does u_ε(x) converge to x/|x| on Ω\{0} as ε→0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.3 ([26, Open Problem 30]). Assume p > 2 and let uε be any minimizer (resp., critical point) of Eε,p on W1,p_g(Ω; R2). Does uε(x) → x/|x| in Ω \ {0} as ε → 0?

accepted.question_text: Consider smooth maps u:R^2→R^2≈C solving Δu=u(1-|u|^2) on R^2 and satisfying |u(x)|→1 as |x|→∞. For each integer q, let V_q(r,θ)=e^{iqθ}g_q(r), where g_q is the unique radial profile with g_q(0)=0 and g_q(r)→1 as r→∞, and let deg(u,∞) be the degree at infinity. Must every such solution u be of the form αV_q(x-x_0) for some q=deg(u,∞), some α∈C with |α|=1, and some translation x_0∈R^2?

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem is whether the functions Vq, q ∈ Z, are the only solutions of (2.4)-(2.5); more precisely: Open Problem 2.4 ... Let u be any solution of (2.4)-(2.5). Does u coincide with Vq modulo rotation and translation, where q = deg(u,∞)?

accepted.question_text: Let u:R^2→R^2 be a smooth solution of Δu=u(1-|u|^2) on R^2 such that |u(x)|→1 as |x|→∞. Must u automatically satisfy the finite-potential-energy condition ∫_{R^2}(|u|^2-1)^2<∞?
accepted.context_brief: Finite-energy condition for entire GL solutions

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5 ([25, Problem 2], [13, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.4) and (2.5). Does (2.7) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R^2, let 0<R<1, prescribe boundary data g(x,y)=(Rx,Ry,√(1-R^2)) on ∂Ω, and consider harmonic maps u:Ω→S^2 satisfying Δu_i=u_i|∇u|^2 in Ω and u=g on ∂Ω. The paper exhibits two explicit solutions u and ̃u. Are there any other solutions besides these two?
accepted.context_brief: Harmonic maps from disc to sphere

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3.1 ([22]). Assume that g is given by (3.4). Are there other solutions of (3.1)–(3.3) besides u and ̃u?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω=B^3 be the unit ball in R^3, let g:∂Ω≈S^2→S^2 be smooth with degree deg g=0, and consider weak harmonic maps u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2) satisfying Δu_i=u_i|∇u|^2 in Ω and u=g on ∂Ω. Does there always exist at least one solution that is continuous on the closed ball Ω̄?

evidence.quote: Since we will be concerned with the existence of continuous harmonic maps satisfying (4.3), we assume throughout this section that (4.5) deg g = 0. ... Open Problem 4.1 ... Assume that (4.5) holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)–(4.3)?

accepted.question_text: Under the same assumptions as in q_008, consider the variational problem inf{E(u): u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2)∩C(Ω̄)} with E(u)=∫_Ω|∇u|^2. Is this infimum attained by some continuous map?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.2 ([40, 41]). Is the (4.7) Inf{ E(u): u ∈ H1_g(Ω; S2) ∩ C(Ω̄) } achieved?

accepted.question_text: Let R(u) be the relaxed energy for maps u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2), where Ω=B^3, deg g=0, and R is defined by weak H^1 limits of continuous S^2-valued maps with the same boundary trace g. Are minimizers of the relaxed-energy problem min{R(u):u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2)} continuous on Ω̄? At least, is one minimizer continuous?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 ([2]). Are the minimizers of (4.9) continuous on Ω̄? (Is it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

accepted.question_text: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed-energy problem min{R(v): v∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2)} on Ω=B^3 with deg g=0. Must the singular interaction term vanish, i.e. is S(u)=0? Equivalently, is the distributional Jacobian Ju equal to 0, or equivalently does there exist a sequence of continuous maps u_n∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2)∩C(Ω̄) converging strongly to u in H^1?
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing singular part of relaxed minimizers

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.4. Let u be a minimizer of (4.9). Is it true that S(u) = 0, i.e., Ju = 0? or equivalently that there exists a sequence (un) in H1_g(Ω; S2) ∩ C(Ω̄) such that un converges to u strongly in H1?

accepted.question_text: For 1<p≤2 and maps f∈W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1), does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f|≤c(p-1)∫_{S^1}∫_{S^1}|f(x)-f(y)|^p/|x-y|^2\,dx\,dy?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.1 ([17, Remark 7]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that, for every 1 < p ≤ 2, (5.2) |deg f| ≤ c (p − 1) ∫∫ |f(x) − f(y)|^p / |x − y|^2 ... ?

accepted.question_text: For continuous circle-valued maps f:S^1→S^1, Theorem 5.2 gives an estimate |deg f|≤C∫∫_{S^1×S^1} 1_{\{|f(x)-f(y)|≥\sqrt{3}\}}/|x-y|^2\,dx\,dy. Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of this theorem? What is the optimal constant C in that estimate, and is that optimal constant attained?
accepted.context_brief: Geometric proof and sharp constant for degree estimate

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.2 ([26, Open Problem 18]). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of Theorem 5.2? What is the best constant C in (5.3)? Is it achieved?

accepted.question_text: For continuous maps f:S^1→S^1 and I_δ(f)=∫∫_{S^1×S^1}1_{\{|f(x)-f(y)|≥δ\}}/|x-y|^2\,dx\,dy, does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f|≤c·δ·I_δ(f) for every 0<δ≤√3?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.3 ([17, Open Problem 3]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that (5.5) |deg f| ≤ c δ Iδ(f) for all f ∈ C(S1; S1) and all δ ≤ √3?

accepted.question_text: For 1<p<∞ and integer degree d, let m_{p,d}=\inf\{\|f\|_{W^{1/p,p}}^p: f∈W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1), deg f=d\}. Is it true that m_{p,d}=|d|m_{p,1} for every integer d? Is the infimum defining m_{p,d} achieved? If the linearity formula fails, is there nevertheless an explicit formula for lim_{d→∞} m_{p,d}/d = \inf_{d>0} m_{p,d}/d?
accepted.context_brief: Least nonlocal energy for prescribed degree

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.4 ([26, Open Problems 22 and 23]). Let 1 < p < ∞. Is it true that mp,d = |d| mp,1 for all d ∈ Z? Is the Inf in (5.6) achieved? Assuming that (5.7) does not hold, is there an explicit formula for lim_{d→+∞} mp,d / d = inf_{d>0} mp,d / d?

accepted.question_text: Suppose f and g are circle-valued maps on S^1 with identical Fourier-modulus data |a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)| for all integers n. Is the known positive conclusion deg f=deg g, which holds for f,g∈W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1) and for Hölder maps C^{0,α} with α>1/3, still valid for rougher classes such as W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) with p>3 or C^{0,α}(S^1;S^1) with α≤1/3? The problem remains open even in mixed-regularity cases where one map is above and the other below the 1/3 threshold.
accepted.context_brief: Can one hear the degree threshold

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f, g ∈ W1/p,p(S1;S1) with p > 3 (resp., f, g ∈ C0,α(S1;S1) with α ≤ 1/3)? The problem is open even under the stronger assumption that f ∈ W1/p,p with 2 < p ≤ 3 and g ∈ W1/q,q with q > 3 (resp., f ∈ C0,α with α > 1/3 and g ∈ C0,β with β ≤ 1/3).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, for each p>3, a summation process (σ_{n,ε}) depending only on p such that for every f∈W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) one can recover the degree from the Fourier magnitudes by lim_{ε→0}\sum_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε}=deg f? Likewise, for each Hölder exponent α≤1/3, does there exist such a summation process depending only on α that works for every f∈C^{0,α}(S^1;S^1)?
accepted.context_brief: Uniform summation process for degree recovery

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.6. Given any p > 3 (resp., α ≤ 1/3), does there exist a summation process (σn,ε), depending only on p (resp., α) such that (5.13) holds for every f ∈ W1/p,p (resp., f ∈ C0,α)?

accepted.question_text: Given a specific circle-valued map f∈C(S^1;S^1), or more generally f∈VMO(S^1;S^1), does there always exist some summation process (σ_{n,ε}) that may depend on f and for which lim_{ε→0}\sum_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε}=deg f?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.7. Given any f ∈ C(S1;S1) (resp., f ∈ VMO(S1;S1)), does there exist a summation process (σn,ε) (depending on f) such that (5.13) holds?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a single map f∈C(S^1;S^1), or even f∈VMO(S^1;S^1), such that no summation process whatsoever can recover deg f from the Fourier-modulus data, meaning that for every admissible summation process (σ_{n,ε}) the quantity \sum_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε} fails to converge to deg f as ε→0?
accepted.context_brief: Universal obstruction to Fourier degree recovery

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.8. Does there exist some f ∈ C(S1;S1) (resp., f ∈ VMO(S1;S1)) such that for any summation process (σn,ε), Σ n |an(f)|2 σn,ε does not converge to deg f?

accepted.question_text:
For homotopy classes E_d={f∈H^1(S^2;S^2):deg f=d}, define Dist_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})=\sup_{f∈E_{d_1}}\inf_{g∈E_{d_2}}\|
abla(f-g)\|_{L^2}. Is it true that Dist_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})^2=8π|d_1-d_2| for all integers d_1,d_2? Even more basically, is this distance symmetric in the two classes?
accepted.context_brief: Distance between H1 homotopy classes on S2

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.9 ([27]). Is it true that Dist2_H1 (Ed1, Ed2) = 8π |d1 − d2| for all d1, d2 ∈ Z? ... Even a much easier problem is open: is it true that Dist_H1(Ed1, Ed2) = Dist_H1(Ed2, Ed1) for all d1, d2 ∈ Z?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the closed unit ball in R^N and let f:B→B be a VMO map. Must it be true that for every ε>0 the approximate fixed-point set {x∈B: |f(x)-x|<ε} has positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Brouwer-type fixed points for VMO maps

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.10. Let B be the closed unit ball in RN and let f be a VMO map from B into itself. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the set {x ∈ B : |f(x) − x| < ε} has positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Consider the extremal weak solution u* arising from the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Δu=λf(u) in a bounded smooth domain Ω⊂R^N, with u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, and f:[0,∞)→(0,∞) smooth, increasing, convex, and superlinear at infinity. When N≥10, Ω is a bounded smooth convex domain, and f(u)=e^u, must the extremal solution u* be unbounded? If not for some convex Ω, can one choose another admissible convex increasing superlinear f, possibly depending on Ω, for which u* is unbounded?
accepted.context_brief: Unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.1 ([16, 34]). Assume that Ω is a bounded smooth convex set in RN, N ≥ 10. Let f(u)=eu. Is u* unbounded? If the answer is negative for some domains Ω, can one find other functions f satisfying (6.2)-(6.3) ... such that u* ∉ L∞(Ω)?

accepted.question_text: In the same extremal-solution setting, assume the extremal solution u* is unbounded. What can be said about its blow-up set? In particular, if the domain Ω is convex, does the blow-up set reduce to a single point?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.2 ([16, 34]). Assume u* ∉ L∞(Ω). What can be said about the blow-up set of u*? Does it consist of a single point when Ω is convex?

accepted.question_text: For functions on the N-dimensional torus T^N, N≥2, the paper proves a stronger phase-control estimate in H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} and explains that the same method would follow from the unresolved inequality ||φ-∫φ||_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} ≤ C ||∇φ||_{H^{1/2}+L^1}. Does this estimate hold for every scalar function φ?

evidence.quote: If we try to establish (7.5) by the same method as above we would need to invoke a stronger version of (7.3); namely (7.6) ||φ − ∫φ||_{H1/2 + W1,1} ≤ C ||∇φ||_{H1/2 + L1}. However, such an estimate is still undecided. Open Problem 7.1 ([4]). Does (7.6) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in R^N, N≥2, let f be smooth on Ω̄, and let U be the unique minimizer in BV(Ω)∩L^2(Ω) of Φ(u)=∫_Ω|∇u| + (1/2)∫_Ω|u-f|^2. Does the distributional gradient ∇U itself belong to BV(Ω)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8.1 ([20, Open Problem 1]). Does ∇U belong to BV(Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded connected domain in R^N, let p≥1, and for a measurable function u:Ω→R define Φ_{λ,p}(u)=meas{(x,y)∈Ω×Ω : |u(x)-u(y)|^p / |x-y|^{p+N} ≥ λ}. The paper proves that if λΦ_{λ,p}(u)→0 as λ→∞, then u is constant. Does the same conclusion still follow from the weaker condition liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,p}(u)=0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.1 ([33, Open Problem 1]). Assume that u satisfies lim inf_{λ→∞} λ Φ_{λ,p}(u) = 0 for some p ≥ 1. Can one conclude that u is a constant?

accepted.question_text: With Φ_{λ,p}(u) defined as in q_026, is there for each 1<p<∞ a constant C=C(p,N,Ω) such that every measurable u satisfies ||∇u||_{L^p}^p ≤ C liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,p}(u), interpreting the left side as +∞ when u∉W^{1,p}(Ω)? Similarly, for p=1, is there a constant C=C(N,Ω) such that the total variation mass ||∇u||_M is bounded by C liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,1}(u), with +∞ if u∉BV(Ω)?
accepted.context_brief: Recovering Sobolev or BV norm from tail functional

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.2 ([32, Section 7.2]). Given any 1 < p < ∞, is there a constant C = C(p,N,Ω) such that ... ||∇u||^p_{Lp} ≤ C lim inf_{λ→∞} λ Φ_{λ,p}(u)? ... Similarly for p = 1, is there a constant C = C(N,Ω) such that ... ||∇u||_M ≤ C lim inf_{λ→∞} λ Φ_{λ,1}(u)?

accepted.question_text: Do the functionals λΦ_{λ,p} Γ-converge, as λ→∞, to the Sobolev or BV energy: namely to u↦c_p||∇u||_{L^p}^p on W^{1,p}(Ω) and +∞ outside W^{1,p}(Ω) when p>1, and to u↦c_1||∇u||_M on BV(Ω) and +∞ outside BV(Ω) when p=1, for some positive constants c_p and c_1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.3 ([32, Section 7.3]). Does the family of functionals λΦ_{λ,p} converge as λ → ∞, in the sense of Γ-convergence, to the functional Ψ defined ... by cp ||∇u||^p_{Lp} on W1,p and +∞ otherwise, and for p = 1 by c1 ||∇u||M on BV and +∞ otherwise?

accepted.question_text: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N, N≥3, and for 0≤t≤1 define f_N(t)=\inf\{P(S): S\subset Q measurable, |S|=t\}, where P(S) is the relative perimeter inside Q. Is there an explicit formula for f_N(t) analogous to the known two-dimensional formula for the square? In particular, is f_N(t) identically equal to 1 for t near 1/2?
accepted.context_brief: Relative isoperimetric profile of the cube

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10.1 ([21]). Is there a formula similar to (10.2) for fN(t) when N ≥ 3? In particular, is it true that fN(t) ≡ 1 near t = 1/2?

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to DOI 10.4171/RLM/1008, then to the EMS Press article page and open-access PDF; mapped sections 1 through 10 and located explicit Open Problem labels on pages 1, 3-6, 8-25.
Extracted explicit problem statements Open Problem 1.1 through Open Problem 10.1 from the article body; all candidates were stated explicitly in the chosen PDF source.

Rewrote each extracted item into a self-contained question by inlining the ambient domain, PDE or variational problem, boundary conditions, and any named quantities needed to understand the question without referring back to the source.
No near-duplicate problem statements were merged; the article presents 29 distinct numbered open problems.

All accepted items are backed by verbatim quotes from the PDF with page citations, and each rewrite avoids unresolved references to section numbers, theorem numbers, or source-only notation without definition.
Saved exact JSON payload to outputs/parse-paper/some-of-my-favorite-open-problems.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
